name: Scotts Bluff National Monument
author: parks-page-legacy
summary: Scotts Bluff National Monument in western Nebraska preserves a prominent natural landmark along the North Platte River that served as a major waypoint on the Oregon Trail, California Trail, and Mormon Trail during the great westward migrations of the 19th century. The bluff, rising 800 feet above the river valley, was visible for miles and marked the passage through a gap in the series of steep bluffs that forced travelers to find specific routes through the terrain. An estimated 250,000 emigrants passed through Mitchell Pass at the base of the bluff between the 1840s and 1860s, and deep wagon wheel ruts are still visible today. The monument was established in 1919 and includes a museum with one of the finest collections of watercolors by pioneer artist William Henry Jackson.
